title: "Coastal blue carbon"
format: html

## Purpose

Value the carbon held in the world's three mapped coastal blue-carbon habitats (mangrove, salt
marsh and seagrass) as part of Gross Ecosystem Product. The quantity is mapped habitat area
multiplied by a per-habitat carbon density. The price is the same annual rental social cost of
carbon that terrestrial carbon storage is valued at [@parisa2022]. The service values storage
only. The figure it reports is the carbon standing in the base year, not a flow between years.

## Source

The write-up is `Global_Climate_Regulation_Coastal_Carbon.docx` in the shared folder of current
write-ups (version of 28 October 2026). The authors' current code is the `develop_yanxu` branch at
`eff0d0b` (2 September 2026). The later `ef89219` leaves the module unchanged. The library takes
two changes from it: soil carbon to the top 30 cm, and the GlobalSeagrass 2019-2020 extent with
one density per pool. The library keeps its own habitat coverage for mangrove and salt marsh and
leaves out the authors' price sensitivities, so those two differ from `eff0d0b` by design.

## Method

### Extent

Each habitat comes from its own published extent map:

| Habitat | Extent |
|---|---|
| Mangrove | Global Mangrove Watch v3, 2019, polygons [@bunting2018; @bunting2022] |
| Salt marsh | GLC_FCS30D 2019, a 30 m land-cover product, with the marsh class extracted to polygons in `global_salt_marsh2019.gpkg` [@zhang2024] |
| Seagrass | GlobalSeagrass 2019-2020, 299 tiles of 10 m presence (`seagrass_extent_dir_path`) [@peng2026; @peng2026data] |

The seagrass tiles are the Zenodo record's `GlobalSeagrass2019_2020.zip` unzipped. The archive's
md5 is in `seagrass_extent_md5`. Each tile is one byte band in EPSG:4326, 1 where seagrass is
mapped and no data elsewhere. They replace the UNEP-WCMC v7.1 polygons [@unepwcmc2021] the
library used before, whose overlapping polygons inflated the seagrass extent.

Seagrass is optional at the tree level (`include_seagrass`). A tree built with seagrass but no
extent file raises rather than running, so a data gap cannot quietly understate the coastal
total. A tree built without seagrass writes every seagrass column at zero, so the combined table
has the same shape either way.

### Aggregation surface

Coastal habitat is aggregated on the **marine** surface, `eemarine_r566` (one row per exclusive
economic zone and coastal region) rather than on the land country surface the other services
use. All 566 rows are measured, and the country table values the `_EEZ` rows (below).

**Mangrove and salt marsh area.** Each polygon layer is clipped to every marine region in turn,
and the clipped pieces are measured in the equal-area projection EPSG:6933 (NSIDC EASE-Grid 2.0
Global), which is what turns polygon geometry into hectares. This is the area the tables report.

**Seagrass area.** The area is measured on the 10 m source grid. A mapped pixel belongs to every
marine region that holds its centre (the rasterisation's `all_touched=False`), and its area is the
area of its row's cell on the WGS84 ellipsoid (`hb.ha_per_cell_rows`, which agrees with pyproj's
geodesic area of the same cell within 1.4e-9 on the rows tested). The r566 regions do not overlap one another, so a
pixel should fall in at most one, but the pass does not assume it: a pixel in two regions is
counted in both, and the table reports, per region, the part another region also holds
(`overlap_ha`). The tile table reports per tile the hectares mapped, the hectares some region
holds counted once, and the overlap-counted hectares. The `_EEZ` rows are by construction the
authors' areas, which assign the same pixels by the same rule to the same EEZ polygons. On three
tiles run through both passes, the densest among them, the EEZ hectares agree within 2.5e-11.

### Carbon density

Density is resolved per pixel for mangrove and salt marsh, and is one value per pool for
seagrass. Every pool is reported in Mg C per hectare. Soil carbon throughout is the stock in the
top `coastal_carbon_soil_depth_cm` (30 cm). The mangrove and salt marsh soil products, and the
latitude fallbacks below, report the top `coastal_carbon_soil_source_depth_cm` (100 cm) and are
taken as a linear share of that profile, 30/100. The seagrass soil density is already a top-30 cm
value and is used as it is.

**Mangrove.** Above-ground biomass follows the Hamilton & Friess latitude regression
[@hamilton2018], AGB (t/ha) = −6.4305 × |lat| + 271.747, floored at zero (the line crosses zero at
roughly 42°, and the floor is what stops it going negative beyond that). Below-ground biomass is
AGB times the
IPCC zone-specific root-to-shoot ratio [@ipcc2014]: 0.49 in the wet tropics, 0.29 in the dry
tropics, 0.96 subtropical, with the tropical boundary at |lat| = 23.5° and the wet/dry split at
2000 mm mean annual precipitation. Biomass converts to carbon at 0.48 for AGB [@hamilton2018] and
0.39 for BGB [@howard2014]. Soil carbon is read from the Sanderman 30 m mangrove soil map
[@sanderman2018]. Where no precipitation raster is supplied the whole tropics take the wet ratio.
Where no soil raster is supplied, soil falls back to a latitude step function for the top 1 m,
400 Mg C/ha within 10° of the equator down to 250 Mg C/ha poleward of 25°, which at 30 cm is 120
down to 75 Mg C/ha.

**Salt marsh.** Above-ground biomass is the Chmura median of 5 t/ha [@chmura2003], raised by a
factor of 1.2 below |lat| = 25° for tropical productivity. Below-ground biomass is 2.5 times AGB,
for the extensive root systems of tidal marsh. Carbon fractions are 0.45 for AGB and 0.41
for BGB. Soil carbon is read from the Maxwell MarSOC map of tidal marsh soils [@maxwell2024]. The
fallback step function runs the other way from mangrove, 180 Mg C/ha for the top 1 m within 20°
of the equator up to 350 Mg C/ha poleward of 45°, which at 30 cm is 54 up to 105 Mg C/ha.

**Seagrass.** The extent records presence only, with no genus or meadow type, so every mapped
pixel takes the same densities. Biomass carbon is the Gomis global mean, 1.55 Mg C/ha
(`seagrass_biomass_c_mg_per_ha`) [@gomis2025], split 30% above ground and 70% below
(`seagrass_agb_fraction`): 0.465 and 1.085 Mg C/ha. Soil carbon is 24.2 Mg C/ha
(`seagrass_soil_c_mg_per_ha`), the Krause global median for the top 30 cm [@krause2025]. The
total is 25.75 Mg C/ha.

### Stock

For mangrove and salt marsh, stock is accumulated pixel by pixel on the 10 arc-second grid. Each
pixel's density is evaluated at its latitude, multiplied by the hectares of habitat in that cell,
and added to the marine region it falls in. The hectares are the cell's area times the share of
the cell the habitat covers, measured by burning the polygons on a grid ten times finer in each
direction (so to 1/100 of a cell). A pixel counts only where that share is positive, a region id
is present and the cell has area. A no-data pixel inside a soil raster contributes zero soil
rather than a missing value, and its biomass still counts. The pass runs in row blocks and skips
any block the habitat does not reach.

For seagrass, stock is each region's mapped hectares multiplied by each pool's density.

Every habitat therefore reports four columns per region: above-ground, below-ground and soil
carbon, and their sum. The total is always the three pools added, never a separately computed
figure, so it cannot drift away from the parts it is printed beside.

### Price and valuation

The price is the annual rental social cost of carbon for the base year, read from the carbon
price series (`carbon_prices.xlsx`) under the run's price convention, the same series and
convention terrestrial carbon uses, so the two carbon services are priced identically. GEP is
then

$$
\text{GEP}_{\text{coastal carbon}} = \text{carbon stock (Mg C)} \times \text{rental SCC (\$ per Mg C)}
$$

applied pool by pool, so the written table carries a value for above-ground, below-ground and soil
carbon as well as the habitat total. The year and the price used travel in the table beside the
values.

### Collapse to one row per country

The service produces two tables. The first, `gep_by_country_base_year_r566`, is the full marine
surface: per-habitat area, stock pools and storage values for each of the r566 marine regions,
with a matching GeoPackage for mapping. Regions with no coastal habitat at all are dropped from
it, they are ocean rows, not zero-value countries.

The second, `gep_by_country_base_year`, is the country table. Building it takes two steps that
each guard against counting the same coast twice:

1. **Keep the `_EEZ` rows.** The marine surface carries a country's coast more than once, as an
   EEZ row plus land and territorial rows over the same habitat. Only the `_EEZ` rows are valued.
2. **Collapse through the canonical r264 row.** The r264 correspondence splits large countries
   into sub-regions (China ×6, India ×6, and four two-way splits), so it is filtered to
   `ee_r264_label == iso3_r250_label` before the join. Without that filter the join repeats a
   split country once per sub-region and the sum multiplies its value. Countries with no coastal
   habitat report zero rather than dropping out.

## Open question: EEZ-only versus all rows

Step 1 above is a choice, not a cleanup. Valuing every r566 row instead of the `_EEZ` rows returns
a strictly larger total, and the gap is exactly the non-EEZ rows, the same coastal habitat
counted again under a land or territorial label. The two totals answer different questions. What
the module writes is the EEZ-only figure. The all-rows figure is what summing the r566 table
gives, and the module does not compute it. The arithmetic of the distinction is pinned in
`test_eez_only_is_a_strict_subset_of_all_rows`.

## Sensitivity worth naming

The latitude fallbacks, mangrove soil without the Sanderman raster, salt marsh soil without
MarSOC, and the mangrove root ratio without a precipitation raster, change the number a run
produces. Which source each run used is written to the log at the point the raster is aligned.

## Outputs

Per habitat, in the habitat's own task directory:

- `<habitat>_area_by_countries2019.{gpkg,csv}`, hectares per marine region. The seagrass table
  also carries `overlap_ha`, and `seagrass_tiles2019.csv` holds the per-tile figures. The seagrass
  tables are written only after the last tile, under temporary names renamed into place.
- `<habitat>_carbon_stock_by_countries2019.csv`, the four stock pools per marine region (Mg C).
- `<habitat>_storage_value_by_countries2019.csv`, the stock pools priced (USD), with the year and
  the rental SCC used.

Then, across habitats:

- `combined_ecosystem_areas.csv`, every habitat's area and stock on one row per marine region,
  plus total coastal area and total carbon stock.
- `gep_by_country_base_year_r566.{csv,gpkg}`, the marine-surface GEP detail.
- `gep_by_country_base_year.csv`, one row per country, the service's GEP result.

## Coverage

The published table is one row for each of the account's 250 countries, base year 2019, in 2019
USD, at the 2019 rental rate of \$13.19 per Mg C. 170 carry a value, totalling
\$6,593,296,170.32, and 80 are zero, every one a country with no EEZ row. None is missing. The table comes from a run on the current
configuration, soil to 30 cm and the 2019-2020 seagrass map, on 2 November 2026.

## Reproduction

The authors' submitted per-country file matches the library's EEZ-side areas for mangrove and
salt marsh in all 250 countries, within 3e-8 ha. With their seagrass extent and soil depth, the
library's EEZ seagrass hectares equal their file in every country, 13,431,380.650 ha in total,
within the 1.4e-9 by which the two pixel-area formulas differ. The library's total is
\$6,593,296,170.32 against their \$6,596,701,698.48, 0.052 percent lower. The gap is in mangrove
and salt marsh, with the sign and size of the coverage difference below.

## What is open

- Mangrove and salt marsh coverage. The library measures the share of a cell each habitat covers
  on a grid ten times finer, and the authors' `eff0d0b` computes the exact polygon share of each
  cell. The two give different hectares in the stock, and the difference stays open. It is not a
  tolerance.
- The price sensitivities at 1, 1.5, 2.5 and 3 percent in the authors' table are not computed.
- The overlaps (review decision 13). Spawn biomass is positive at sampled mangrove points, so
  mangrove biomass may also be counted in terrestrial carbon, but that overlap is not quantified.
  Whether and how the account nets it out is open, together with the EEZ-only scope above. The
  overlapping UNEP-WCMC polygons are no longer read.
- The salt marsh soil raster (MarSOC) and the precipitation raster are configured but are in
  neither the laptop base_data nor the MSI one, so a run there uses the latitude fallback for salt
  marsh soil and the wet-tropics ratio for mangrove roots, as before.
